agents.note: Sprint 63 (V0.29.17) US-489 DONE (passes:true) 2/4 -- Iris polish P-1, System Status glanceability. THE JUDGEMENT CALL IS THE STORY: a summary line is a LOSSY COMPRESSION of four tiles, so it is exactly where a green-when-broken lie enters -- but the naive reading of AC-1 (green only if all 4 == ok) produces the OPPOSITE dishonesty. DRIVE=IDLE is the only `neutral` this card emits and means 'not recording', not 'broken'; requiring drive==ok makes green UNREACHABLE in the commonest state (key on, no drive started) -> the line reads amber forever and the operator learns to ignore it. Crying wolf is a dishonest instrument too. So: THREE buckets. ok=good; neutral=nominal-inactive (does not block green, is not an issue); unavailable=known-UNKNOWN (BLOCKS green -- never claim OK over a source we cannot read -- but renders MUTED grey, not amber, because nothing is broken); amber/down=the only ISSUES. FAIL-CLOSED on vocabulary: an unrecognised level ranks as unavailable, never ok, so a future tile level cannot paint the card green by default (pinned with a junk level). Line = glanceable COUNT ('SYSTEM · OK' / '· 1 ISSUE' / '· 2 ISSUES' / '· 1 UNAVAILABLE'), detail = the WORST source NAMED ('OBD LINK · RECONNECTING') -- both AC-1 example forms render, and the operator gets count + what-to-look-at without reading four tiles. Worst-wins not first-wins; a real issue always outranks an unknown so an unreadable source can never mask a known fault. SSOT: summary computed from the SAME tiles object the grid renders (test asserts view.summary == systemSummary(view.tiles)) so headline and grid cannot disagree. DOT -- DO NOT 'FIX' THIS: AC-3's parenthetical lists '(green/amber/red/neutral)' but the operative clause is MIRRORING the existing per-tile level, and after US-488/TD-067 there IS no red in this card's mapping. I mirrored faithfully (down->amber) and refused to invent a red dot: it would re-open TD-067 one sprint after I closed 8/10 of it AND contradict the amber number beside it. Test asserts dot and value resolve to the SAME token for `down`. SCOPE FENCE (the trap): appendTile is SHARED with the idle, battery and LTFT cards -> dot is OPT-IN (3rd arg), or three shipped cards restyle from a story scoped to one. Also spelled `.sys-grid .tile:last-child` out explicitly -- the base rule zeroes border-bottom there and the last grid cell would render open-sided. CROSS-FILE CATCH, FOURTH SPRINT RUNNING: grid/dot/summary are classes the JS must EMIT; a CSS-only change styles markup that never renders, silently. Guards assert the renderer emits each class, tags the summary with data-level, and appends the 4 tiles into `grid` and NOT `body`. REAL HARNESS BUG FOUND (not production): the node probe used subprocess text=True with NO encoding, so Python decoded node's UTF-8 with the Windows locale codepage and '·' came back as 'Â·' -- it failed as a one-char diff that looks exactly like a bad production string. Cost me a cycle. Fixed in my file (encoding='utf-8'); 5 sibling helpers share the omission but all their assertions are ASCII so it is LATENT -> filed TD-068 instead of widening the diff. Next person asserting non-ASCII copy gets bitten unless TD-068 lands. GREEN in-loop: 32 new; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 199 passed; ruff clean. black+mypy still not installed on this Windows host (standing gap). PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED (480x320, the card is deliberately re-laid-out): 2x2 must not overflow at 480px with the longest tile values; 17px summary must read at a glance; a parked/OBD-off state must show a MUTED 'SYSTEM · 1 UNAVAILABLE' -- not amber, not green. NEXT AVAILABLE: US-490 (context-aware menu access, S) -- the vertical-dots button shows only on the parked/idle home card, hidden while driving, 5s long-press always. Note it keys off the SAME emitter `idle` SSOT boolean US-481 introduced (carouselIdle in carousel.js) -- do not re-derive idle from the drive-state string.
